title: Smooth approximation of valued generic points at index one
statement: Let $R\hookrightarrow A$ be an injective local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}A$, and suppose $\mathfrak m_RA=\mathfrak m_A$ and $\kappa(A)/\kappa(R)$ is separable, including the possibly transcendental meaning of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $W$ be a smooth finite-type $K$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $w:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W$ be a $K$-morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist a smooth affine finite-type $R$-scheme $U$, an $R$-morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$, and a $K$-morphism $h:U_K\to W$ such that $h\circ a_K=w$, where $U_K=U\times_R\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $a_K$ is the restriction of $a$ [def-pc-base-change]. No excellence, completeness or separability of $L/K$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR 3.6 Proposition 4, printed p.79 (PDF p.85), as used in 7.2 Theorem 1 proof, printed pp.176–177 (PDF pp.182–183): first choose an affine finite-type model of the generic point, then smooth it along the valued point. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent formulation where explicitly indicated.

proof.text: Choose $\pi$ as in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. From the finite affine cover in the definition of finite type choose $V=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset W$ containing the image of $w$; $C$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra and $w$ is an algebra map $\psi:C\to L$. Choose generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ and integers $n_i\geq0$ with $\pi^{n_i}\psi(c_i)\in A$ (a uniformizer of $A$ is $\pi$). In $C$ set $B_0=R[\pi^{n_1}c_1,\ldots,\pi^{n_r}c_r]$. The restriction $\varphi_0=\psi|_{B_0}$ lands in $A$. This algebra is finite type, multiplication by $\pi$ is injective since it is invertible in $C$, and $B_0[1/\pi]=C$: each $c_i=\pi^{-n_i}(\pi^{n_i}c_i)$ and $K=R[1/\pi]$. Its generic spectrum is therefore $V$, which is smooth by restriction of the smooth structure of $W$. The generic-fibre identification uses $B_0\otimes_RK\cong B_0[1/\pi]$, with $b\otimes(r/\pi^n)\mapsto rb/\pi^n$ and inverse $b/\pi^n\mapsto b\otimes\pi^{-n}$.

source.place: BLR 7.2 Theorem 1 proof, printed p.176 (PDF p.182), choice of a model in an affine neighbourhood; explicit scaled-generator construction by Q108

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-index-one-differential-defect-criterion] to $(B_0,\varphi_0)$ and write $d=\delta_{B_0}(\varphi_0)\in\mathbf N$. Inductively construct $(B_j,\varphi_j)$ for $0\leq j\leq d$, with compatible inclusions into $C$, generic algebra $C$, injective multiplication by $\pi$, and $\delta_{B_j}(\varphi_j)\leq\max\{0,d-j\}$. The base case is the preceding step. For the induction step take $I_j=\ker(B_j\to A\to\kappa(A))$ and $B_{j+1}=B_j[I_j/\pi]$. The dilatation estimate [lem-sfb-index-one-residue-dilatation-defect-drop] supplies finite type, injectivity of $\pi$, unchanged generic algebra, the compatible map $\varphi_{j+1}$, and $\delta_{j+1}\leq\max\{0,\delta_j-1\}\leq\max\{0,d-(j+1)\}$. All its hypotheses persist, including smooth generic spectrum $V$; the DVR extension and residue extension stay fixed. Thus $\delta_{B_d}(\varphi_d)=0$. This also covers $d=0$ with no dilatation.

source.place: BLR 3.6 paragraph before Proposition 3, Proposition 3, and the finite iteration yielding Proposition 4, printed p.79 (PDF p.85)

proof.text: The criterion [lem-sfb-index-one-differential-defect-criterion] applied to $(B_d,\varphi_d)$ gives $f\in B_d$ with $\varphi_d(f)$ a unit and $U=\operatorname{Spec}(B_d[1/f])$ smooth over $R$. It is affine and finite type: generators for $B_d$, together with $1/f$, generate its coordinate algebra. The unit condition extends $\varphi_d$ to $B_d[1/f]\to A$, giving $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_K=\operatorname{Spec}(B_d[1/f]\otimes_RK)=\operatorname{Spec}(C[1/f])$ (as $B_d[1/f]\otimes_RK=B_d[1/f][1/\pi]$ and $B_d[1/\pi]=C$) and $a_K$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $B_d[1/f]\otimes_RK\to A\otimes_RK=A[1/\pi]$. The generic-fibre map $U_K=\operatorname{Spec}(C[1/f])\to\operatorname{Spec}C=V\subset W$ defines $h$ (here $f$ denotes its image in $C$). On rings the composite $C\to C[1/f]\to L$ is exactly $\psi$, because every $\varphi_j$ restricts to $\varphi_0$ and the generic inclusions identify $B_j[1/\pi]$ with $C$. Hence $h\circ a_K=w$. Here $A[1/\pi]=L$ since $\pi$ generates $\mathfrak m_A$, so this generic restriction has domain $\operatorname{Spec}L$ as required.
